background: CaixaBank is Spain's largest domestic bank by loans and deposits, formed from the la Caixa savings bank and its takeover of Bankia, with a retail, insurance and asset-management franchise concentrated in Spain and Portugal.
synthesis: The bank is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, all three on a stable outlook, and the latest move was a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 8 Jul 2026. Capital is the weak side against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 12.3% is in the bottom quarter and leverage of 5.5% sits at the median. Liquidity is a real strength, with LCR of 193% and NSFR of 143% both in the top quarter, though LCR has fallen 14 points and NSFR 6 points since 30 Jun 2025. The flagged news is good: first-half profit up 8.5% on 29 Jul 2026, and the rating upgrade before that.
